append.text: **Ps 30:2 and 30:17 — the Te Deum line, decided here as D15 foresaw:** *In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum* → *Em vós, Senhor, esperei: para sempre não serei envergonhado*; 30:17 *Dómine, non confúndar* → *Senhor, não serei envergonhado* (one decision, `confundar`). *confúndar* is future and present subjunctive at once; the Greek has the optative (μὴ καταισχυνθείην) both times and DRB / MS1932 take the wish — the future is ruled, as 24:1 *não corarei*, with D23's formula for the negated *in ætérnum*. The blind reader heard 'never be put to shame'; the Latinist passed both places twice. The stylist asked *não serei envergonhado para sempre* (the 'not for ever' order, refused; option). Options: *jamais*, the wish *não seja eu envergonhado*, the traditional *confundido*. = 70:1 and the Te Deum's close (Common/Prayers.txt).

Ps 30:18 *Erubéscant ímpii* → *Corem os ímpios*, one verse after *não serei envergonhado* (confúndi) — the Latin's two verbs kept two. **The blind reader listed *Corem* as unknown (again).** *Envergonhem-se* is the option in Ps 30.
Ps 30:3 *accélera ut éruas me* (no source) → *apressai-vos a libertar-me*, the row's proposal (libertar without a source); passed the Latinist twice, no reader remark.
Ps 30:16 *Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum* → *Arrancai-me da mão dos meus inimigos* (a source named); no reader remark.

**Ps 30:6 *redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis* → *vós me resgatastes, Senhor, Deus da verdade*** — weighed against *remistes*, as this row asked: *remir* is safe in the perfect and is the Redeemer's verb, but the imperatives cannot take it (*remi-me*), so it would split one Latin verb (λυτρόομαι) in two. Serves the Compline responsory's versicle *Redemísti nos* (*Vós nos resgatastes*). Passed the Latinist twice; *remistes* is the option (decision `redemisti`).

**Ps 30:17 *Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum* → *Iluminai a vossa face sobre o vosso servo*** — illustráre (only here) is the same Greek as 118:135 (ἐπίφανον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἐπὶ τὸν δοῦλόν σου, both in Rahlfs), so D15's test merges them and the colon is 118:135a word for word (formula row). The stylist asked *Fazei brilhar* for the third time (refused, option); the blind reader paraphrased it rightly; the Latinist passed it twice.

**Ps 30:21 *Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ* → *Vós os escondereis no lugar escondido da vossa face*** — as this row asked; the psalm's four abscond- words are all *esconder* (30:5, 20, 21 ×2). The blind reader heard 'a secret shelter of God' first; passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 30:25 *Viríliter ágite* → *Portai-vos como homens*** — applied as proposed (*Agi* is 'I acted'); the blind reader heard 'be brave' first, 'as males' second. Passed the Latinist twice; no stylist remark.
Ps 30:25 *et confortétur cor vestrum* → *e que o vosso coração se fortaleça* (26:14 in the plural).

**Ps 30:12 *et vicínis meis valde* → *e sobremaneira para os meus vizinhos*** — a local departure. Draft 1 *e muito para os meus vizinhos* was the stylist's worst line (*muito* hangs, not tied to *afronta*) and the blind reader could hear 'many neighbours'; draft 2 *sobretudo* (MS1932) was marked MAJOR by the Latinist gate (a comparison the Latin does not make) and his *sobremaneira* was taken verbatim (draft 3, unread). Where *valde* bears on a dative or stands at the end of a member, *muito* may need this help; *grandemente* is the option.
Ps 30:8 *respexísti humilitátem meam* → *olhastes para a minha humilhação*; the blind reader heard 'the shame I suffered' first, the low state second.
Ps 30:8 *salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam* → *salvastes a minha alma das necessidades*; the blind reader heard privations, 'difficulties and want' — near the straits again.

Ps 30:7 *Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue* → *Vós odiais os que observam vaidades, * em vão*: the blind reader heard 'pay attention to futile things' first, practices without value second, conceit third. Kept (the row); *coisas vãs* is the option in Ps 30.
Ps 30:7 — alone after the asterisk (*em vão*); whether it goes with *odiais* or with *observam* stays open, as in the Latin (the blind reader heard both).
Ps 30:7 *Odísti* (God) → *Vós odiais* — the present sense (24:19, 25:5); passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 30:5 *Edúces me de láqueo hoc* → *Vós me tirareis deste laço* (tirar de with a source, 29:4).
Ps 30:9 *statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos* → *firmastes os meus pés num lugar espaçoso* — the stylist's best line of Ps 30.
Ps 30:9 *in loco spatióso* → *num lugar espaçoso*, as this row reserved.

Ps 30:21b *a contradictióne linguárum* → *da contenda das línguas*: the blind reader listed *contenda* as unknown and still heard 'quarrels and attacks in words'. The echo *tenda … contenda* in one verse is accepted (neither at the same cadence).

Ps 30:22 *mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi* → *fez maravilhosa a sua misericórdia para mim*: the stylist again called the build a calque (*mostrou de modo maravilhoso*, refused, option); the blind reader did not stumble; passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 30:20 *Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ* → *Como é grande, Senhor, a multidão da vossa doçura*: the blind reader heard people first ('multidão' suggests a crowd), quantity at once after.
Ps 30:20 → *a multidão da vossa doçura* (the Epiphany II responsory, Tempora/Epi2-1.txt).

Ps 30:20b *Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te* → *Vós a aperfeiçoastes para os que esperam em vós* — the object (30:20's *quam*, the sweetness) supplied as a pronoun because the verse stands alone; heard rightly.

Ps 30:12 *factus sum oppróbrium* → *tornei-me uma afronta*; the blind reader heard 'someone who offends' first, 'an object of scorn' second. *Super omnes inimícos meos* → *Mais que todos os meus inimigos* (the Latinist, minor: the comparison).

**Ps 30:11b departs:** *e os meus ossos foram perturbados* — the Latinist marked the state MAJOR here (with 30:10 *conturbátus est … óculus meus*), and the psalm's two conturbáre now share one tense (*na ira foram perturbados o meu olho … e os meus ossos foram perturbados*). 6:3 (*conturbáta sunt ossa mea*, another order) keeps *estão*; the state is option 2 in Ps 30's decision `conturbatus`.

Ps 30:18 *deducántur in inférnum* → *sejam conduzidos ao inferno* — a curse on the wicked, as 9:18; no reader stopped at it. *dedúci in* → *ser conduzido* (the passive of dúcere; D25's *fazer descer* has no sayable passive).
Ps 30:24 *veritátem requíret Dóminus* → *o Senhor procurará a verdade* (MS1932); the blind reader heard 'will investigate the truth' first, 'will seek sincerity in people' second.
Ps 30:11 *defécit in dolóre vita mea* → *a minha vida desfaleceu na dor*; heard as 'lost strength to live'; *desfaleceu* listed as unknown by the blind reader.

terms: | commendáre | entregar (*Nas vossas mãos entrego o meu espírito*) | open | Ps 30:6, only place (grep); παραθήσομαι, 'deposit with'. The plain verb, heard as entrusting at death (the blind reader); loses the deposit. *encomendar* (MS1932, DRB) is 'to order goods' in Brazil; *confiar* heard as 'trust'. Both are options. Serves the Compline responsory and Lk 23:46 (Clementine: *Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum*, fetched). The stylist asked the object first for the proparoxytone *espírito* at the mediant — refused (the responsory's order). |

| enutríre | nutrir (*me guiareis, e me nutrireis*) | open | Ps 30:4; 54:23 *et ipse te enútriet* (grep). διαθρέψεις, the root of 22:2 *educávit me* (ἐξέθρεψεν) → *me nutriu*: one root, one verb. MS1932 *sustentar* the option. |

| conclúdere (a person) | encerrar (*E não me encerrastes nas mãos do inimigo*) | open | Ps 30:9 (συνέκλεισας); 77:50, 77:62 *conclúsit* (in morte, in gládio) will test it; 16:9b *conclusérunt* (their fat) → *fecharam*, another use; 34:3 *conclúde*. MS1932 *entregaste* the option. |

| sortes (*in mánibus tuis sortes meæ*) | as minhas sortes | open | Ps 30:15, only place; the Latin reads 'lots' where the Greek (and the Hebrew) has 'times' (οἱ καιροί μου) — the Latin followed. The blind reader listed *sortes* unknown and heard 'my luck / fate'; singular *a minha sorte* and MS1932 *o meu destino* are options. |

| excéssus mentis / in excéssu meo | fora de mim (*Eu, porém, disse, fora de mim*) | open | Ps 30:23 (ἐν τῇ ἐκστάσει μου); 115:2 *Ego dixi in excéssu meo* and 67:28a *in mentis excéssu* (grep) can follow. The going-out said plainly; *excesso* is 'too much', *êxtase* mystical joy. The blind reader heard 'in despair, not in control' first, 'ecstasy' second; the Latinist passed it twice. Options *no arrebatamento da minha mente*, DRB's *no excesso da minha mente*. |
| vituperátio | censura (*ouvi a censura de muitos*) | open | Ps 30:13, only place (ψόγος); heard as 'criticism' (the blind reader: censorship second). Options *difamação*, *vitupério* |

| consiliári | planejar (*planejaram tomar a minha alma*) | open | Ps 30:14, only place (ἐβουλεύσαντο). Draft 1 *deliberaram* was unknown to the blind reader and 'minutes of a meeting' to the stylist. Stays apart from consílium → conselho / desígnio only by root. |
| abúsio | desprezo (*com soberba e com desprezo*) | open | Ps 30:19, only place (ἐξουδένωσις, the family of abjéctio → desprezo 21:7). *abuso* is misuse. MS1932 |

| oblivióni dare | entregar ao esquecimento (*fui entregue ao esquecimento*) | open | Ps 30:12b; 136:5 *oblivióni detur déxtera mea* (grep). Cost: *entregar* also stands for commendáre in 30:6. Options *fui dado ao esquecimento*, *fui esquecido* (the Greek's) |

| vas pérditum | vaso destruído (*Tornei-me como um vaso destruído*) | open | Ps 30:13, only place (σκεῦος ἀπολωλός; DRB *destroyed*). Draft 1 *vaso perdido* was heard by the blind reader as a vase gone missing. MS1932 *quebrado* the option |

| fácere supérbiam | agir com soberba (*aos que agem com soberba*) | open | Ps 30:24 (the stylist's, for MS1932's *procedem com soberba*); 100:7 *qui facit supérbiam* (grep). *praticar* is operári's |
| supérbia | soberba | working | Ps 16:9b *falou soberba*, 30:19 *com soberba e com desprezo*, 30:24 |

| dedúci in (+ place) | ser conduzido a (*sejam conduzidos ao inferno*) | open | Ps 30:18 (καταχθείησαν, 'brought down'; MS1932 *conduzidos*); the passive is safe from the homograph ban (on the imperative only). D22's *guiar* is guidance; D25's *fazer descer* has no sayable passive |
| commorári | morar (*de muitos que moram ao redor*) | open | Ps 30:13 (παροικούντων); apart from habitáre → habitar |
| abundánter | abundantemente | open | Ps 30:24, only place; the stylist's, for draft 1 *com abundância* (two *com* in one colon) |

| conturbátio | perturbação (*longe da perturbação dos homens*) | open | Ps 30:21, only place; the noun of conturbáre → perturbar. *longe da* for the separating *a* (the stylist), as 30:12b *longe de mim … longe do coração* |
| paupértas | pobreza (*O meu vigor se enfraqueceu na pobreza*) | open | Ps 30:11b, only place (πτωχεία; the Hebrew's 'iniquity' not followed); heard as want of means |
| cívitas muníta / locus munítus | cidade fortificada / lugar fortificado | open | Ps 30:22; 59:11 = 107:11 *in civitátem munítam*, 70:3 *in locum munítum* (grep) |
| ídeo | por isso | working | Ps 30:23b *Ídeo exaudísti* (διὰ τοῦτο; the Hebrew's 'but', MS1932 *Mas*, not followed) |
formulas: | *In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum* (30:2a = 70:1a; the Te Deum's last line, Common/Prayers.txt: *In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum*) | *Em vós, Senhor, esperei: para sempre não serei envergonhado* | open — Ps 30 (decision `confundar`; D15, D23). 70:1 continues *in justítia tua líbera me, et éripe me* |

| *In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis* (30:6; the Compline short responsory, Special/Minor Special.txt: *R.br. In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum. V. Redemísti nos, Dómine, Deus veritátis*; Lk 23:46) | *Nas vossas mãos entrego o meu espírito: vós me resgatastes, Senhor, Deus da verdade* — responsory: *Nas vossas mãos, Senhor, * entrego o meu espírito. V. Vós nos resgatastes, Senhor, Deus da verdade* | open — Ps 30 |

| *Illústra / Illúmina fáciem tuam super servum tuum* (30:17a; 118:135a *Fáciem tuam illúmina super servum tuum*; one Greek, ἐπίφανον) | *Iluminai a vossa face sobre o vosso servo* | open — Ps 30 (= 118:135) |

| *In tua justítia * líbera me, Dómine* (the Monday Sext antiphon, Psalmi minor.txt; from 30:2b) | *Na vossa justiça * livrai-me, Senhor* (the psalm verse says *livrai-me na vossa justiça*) | open — Ps 30 |

| *Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, quam abscondísti timéntibus te … Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te* (30:20–20b; the Epiphany II responsory, Tempora/Epi2-1.txt) | *Como é grande, Senhor, a multidão da vossa doçura, que escondestes para os que vos temem! … Vós a aperfeiçoastes para os que esperam em vós* | open — Ps 30 |

| *Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino* (30:25; a versicle in Sancti/Urbis/11-29; cf. 26:14) | *Portai-vos como homens, e que o vosso coração se fortaleça, todos vós que esperais no Senhor* | open — Ps 30 |

| 30:2–3b ≈ 70:1–3 (*Inclína ad me aurem tuam* 70:2a; *Esto mihi in Deum protectórem* 70:3a, with *in locum munítum* for *in domum refúgii*) | Ps 70 copies Ps 30's words where the Latin is the same: *Inclinai para mim o vosso ouvido*; *Sede para mim um Deus protetor* | open — Ps 30 |
